OCRD CardType='S': Mart 1,247 (Oil 2,222, Bev 1,686). OINV: Mart 25,157 (Oil 30,669, Bev 5,351). OITW: Mart 47,908 (Oil 127,257, Bev 95,349). All four reproduce to the row. claim: `sap distributors` is the VENDOR master (CardType='S'), not distributors

The live payload's first row is VENDA000526 / 10M ANALYTICS / CardType 'S' / Active 'N'; HANA confirms VENDA000526 = 10M ANALYTICS, CardType 'S', GroupCode 105, Balance 0. All seven e-commerce distributors the study names as the real ones are CardType='C' in Mart OCRD (CUSTA000907 SUSTAINQUEST 20.40 L, CUSTA000927 ANTIZE FOODS 50.39 L, CUSTA000900 BABA LOKENATH -1.66 L, CUSTA000354 CHIRAG 29.35 L, CUSTA000906 EVARA 7.85 L, CUSTA000592 KNOWTABLE 2.21 Cr, CUSTA000048 R K WORLDINFOCOM 7.51 Cr). claim: Turnover is not computable from this domain - no credit-note endpoint exists and sales-invoices includes cancelled rows
evidence: Stronger than the study claimed. I scanned all 240 distinct /api/ paths in harvest/reconciled.json (the WHOLE ecom app, not just the sap domain) with /credit|return|orin|rin1|refund/i: ZERO hits. The 17 sap paths contain nothing reading ORIN. HANA: Mart ORIN = 4,444 credit-note documents (the study's figure, exact); Oil 6,385; Bev 430. And OINV CANCELED='Y' = 252 of the 25,157, so sales-invoices really does ship cancelled rows (24,653 clean). Summing DocTotal-VatSum from `sap sales-invoices` therefore overstates by 252 cancelled documents and by 4,444 un-netted credit notes.
impact: None - the gap is real and the warning is correctly worded. Turnover must come from hana_turnover / sapb1, never from this domain.

claim: `DocTotal` here is GST-inclusive, verified at exactly 5%
evidence: SPLIT VERDICT. The GST-INCLUSIVE half is CONFIRMED - the arithmetic reproduces on all three live rows (37594: 9640-459.0465=9180.9535, x5%=459.048; 37603: 6941-330.5255=6610.4745, x5%=330.524; 37601: 2065-98.334=1966.666, x5%=98.333). But 'exactly 5%' does NOT generalise, and the study extrapolated 3 rows to a rule. I bucketed all 25,157 Mart OINV rows by VatSum/(DocTotal-VatSum): exactly 5% = 22,062 rows (87.7%, 303.78 Cr); blended 5-18% = 2,316 rows (15.89 Cr); exactly 12% = 251 rows (1.22 Cr); exactly 18% = 236 rows (14.39 Cr); zero VAT = 63 rows (6.84 Cr); other = 174; degenerate = 55. So 12.3% of Mart invoices are NOT at 5%, and 18% invoices alone carry 14.39 Cr. The reports study (Trap 2) then propagates the error: it says the 1.05 factor is safe because 'the SAP invoices in the sibling domain independently confirm at exactly 5%'.
impact: An operator who back-computes net from DocTotal using /1.05 instead of DocTotal-VatSum is wrong on ~1 invoice in 8, and materially wrong on the 18%-slab invoices. Worse, the reports study uses the claim as cross-domain justification for its own 1.05 arithmetic.
action: Trap 5 should read: 'DocTotal is GST-inclusive; net = DocTotal - VatSum. ALWAYS subtract VatSum - never divide by 1.05. The rate is 5% on 87.7% of Mart invoices (22,062/25,157) but 12% on 251, 18% on 236, zero on 63, and blended on 2,316.' Delete the 'independently confirm at exactly 5%' clause from the reports study's Trap 2 and replace with 'the 5% slab applies to the edible-oil lines here; it is NOT a company-wide rate.'

claim: `sap sales-analysis` takes from_date, to_date, source, main_group, chain, location, sub_group, cardname, page, page_size (10 params)
evidence: The study read only ONE of the three call sites. PlatformSapDashboard-bUN0KEtA.js has M={source,month,year,main_group,chain,location,sub_group,cardname} - which is what the study transcribed. But PlatformSapData-ByaICPCc.js is a second call site for the same endpoint with a much wider filter state, verbatim: C={source:`mart`,from_date:`2026-01-01`,to_date:<today>,search:``,main_group:``,chain:``,state:``,type:``,brand:``,location:``,item_head:``,sub_group:``,sales_person:``,cardname:[]}, plus the dropdown list oe=[[`main_group`],[`chain`],[`state`],[`type`],[`item_head`],[`sub_group`],[`brand`],[`location`],[`sales_person`]]. Its builder spreads the WHOLE state onto the query: function j(e,t){let n={page:t,page_size:b,nocache:1};Object.entries(e).forEach(...n[e]=t)}. And Dashboard-Ci-nVmGI.js is a THIRD call site sending {page:0,page_size:1,from_date,to_date,source:`mart`,item_head:wt,aggregate:`item_head`}. Lens C independently found search/state/type/brand/item_head/sales_person/aggregate and is RIGHT; the study is wrong. Nine params missing: search, state, type, brand, item_head, sales_person, aggregate, nocache, fresh. Also `cardname` is an ARRAY (multi-select) at the PlatformSapData call site, not the scalar the study implies.
impact: The domain's main analysis endpoint would ship with 9 of its 19 filters missing - including `item_head`, which JIVO correction C-0003 makes the CORRECT way to segment PREMIUM/COMMODITY/OTHERS. An operator would be told to name-match instead, which C-0003 explicitly forbids.
action: Spec entry for `sap sales-analysis` must add: `search` (string), `state`, `type`, `brand`, `item_head`, `sales_person` (all free-form, valid values come back in the response `filters` block), `aggregate` (enum: `item_head` - the only value observed), `nocache` (1), `fresh` (1). Mark `cardname` as repeatable/comma-joined. Cite PlatformSapData-ByaICPCc.js and Dashboard-Ci-nVmGI.js as the sources the study missed.

claim: Trap 15: sales-analysis is a bulk endpoint; anything summing it must page to exhaustion or pass a large page_size
evidence: True of the dashboard's call pattern, false as general advice, because the endpoint has a server-side aggregation the study never found. Dashboard-Ci-nVmGI.js verbatim: Be={page:0,page_size:1,from_date,to_date,source:`mart`,item_head:wt,aggregate:`item_head`} then reads s=He.data?.aggregate and iterates it as rows of {item_head, liter, line_total}. That is page_size:1 with the totals computed server-side - the exact opposite of paging to exhaustion. The study's own §4 also inherits CLAUDE.md's 'there is no server-side SUM' assumption, which is true of SAP's OData but not of this endpoint.
impact: A CLI that follows the study's advice pulls up to 100k rows to compute a total the server will return in one row. Slow, and it makes the totals a client-side reimplementation that can drift from the dashboard's.
action: Rewrite Trap 15 as two cases: (a) for row-level analysis the SPA sends page_size=1e5 and totals client-side, so a 50-row default silently truncates; (b) for headline totals pass `aggregate=item_head` with page_size=1 and read the response's `aggregate[]` block - the server aggregates. Mark the `aggregate[]` response shape UNVERIFIED (read from client code; the probe only ever got the 400).

claim: `inventory-overview` `status` is a string whose values were not observed

PlatformSapInventory-DsKqShCV.js verbatim: D=[{value:``,label:`All`},{value:`Y`,label:`Active`},{value:`N`,label:`Frozen`}], and the SPA's default filter state is T={search:``,status:`Y`,stock_state:`in`,warehouse:[],warehouse_code:[],group:[],is_litre:``} - i.e. the dashboard defaults to Active-only. claim: §5: sales-invoice-lines is broken upstream because no table has a column named `UnitMsr`
evidence: Re-ran the schema check myself against SYS.TABLE_COLUMNS for JIVO_MART_HANADB, columns LIKE '%UNITMSR%' in INV1/OITM/OINV. evidence: Verbatim in Reports-C5n-R5Ns.js: le={amazon:`AMAZON`,blinkit:`BLINKIT`,zepto:`ZEPTO`,swiggy:`SWIGGY`,bigbasket:`BIG BASKET`,flipkart:`FLIPKART`,flipkart_grocery:`FLIPKART GROCERY`,zomato:`ZOMATO`,citymall:`CITY MALL`} - 9 entries, the study's transcription exact. claim: Trap 2: the Amazon PO money is GST-exclusive, verified as cost_price 714.29 x 1.05 = 750.00 and amount 3,809.52 x 1.05 = 4,000.00
evidence: Pulled the values out of probe/probe-run1.jsonl myself: cost_price 714.29, requested_qty 412.0, total_requested_cost 294287.48; billing amounts 3809.52, 57142.86, 7619.05. 412 x 714.29 = 294,287.48 EXACT. 714.29x1.05=750.0045, 3809.52x1.05=3999.996, 57142.86x1.05=60000.003, 7619.05x1.05=8000.0025 - all round to the clean figure, so the 'exactly' is 2dp rounding rather than literal, but the GST-exclusive conclusion is sound and the field name total_order_amt_exclusive corroborates it. claim: 25 endpoints written with ZERO live payloads; every response shape marked UNVERIFIED, no shape/field/row-count stated as fact
evidence: Verified the premise: shipment.json status_counts = {GATED:17, UNPROBED:17}, every probe code is 403 (17 of them, no other code), the ONLY probe_reason string in the whole bundle is {"detail":"You do not have access to the Amazon Shipment Planner."}, and live_response is null on all 34 rows - I checked for a non-null and found none. me.json: 144 permissions, is_superuser false, `amazon.shipment_planning.view` absent (it holds sap.view, sap.invoice.view, dispatch.view, admin.dispatch.manage, platform.*.access etc. - 36 dotted perms, none of them the gate). NO row count is stated anywhere in the study for any endpoint - I looked specifically. Field-name discipline is good: 16 of 18 shape mentions are explicitly attributed ('Client reads X', 'Client treats the response as an array', 'suggests those two fields'). TWO soft spots, both minor: (1) the `shipment record` table row states 'with per-line `planned_qty`, `case_pack`, `planned_liters` and a `not_loaded` flag' unhedged before the attributed 'Client reads results[]' - the fields are genuinely in Record-uhJVTCfL.js (I verified b()=Sigma planned_qty, /case_pack, /1e3 planned_liters, and .filter(e=>!e.not_loaded)) so it is accurate but presented as observation rather than client-derived; (2) Trap 6's header 'Fields observed by name' plus its unit annotations (pieces/litres/cartons) is inference dressed as observation - `sap_available` being in pieces is reasoned, not seen.
impact: Small. The blanket UNVERIFIED banner in §4 covers both, so a spec author following the study will not emit a response_path. But an operator skimming §2 could read the `record` row as a promise about the payload.
action: Reword the `shipment record` cell to 'Client reads results[]; the per-line fields it touches are planned_qty, case_pack, planned_liters and not_loaded (client-derived, UNVERIFIED)'. Retitle Trap 6 'Field names read by the client, with inferred units' and mark the unit column inferred.

claim: Param names and enums: truck_size in {10_ton,15_ton,custom}, warehouse in {GP-FGM,BH-FGM,GP-FG,BH-EC,ALL}, 7-value status, 4-value switch_state
evidence: All four read verbatim out of the bundle. CreateShipment-jeq_xTG5.js: at=[{value:`10_ton`,label:`10 Tonnes`,capacity:1e4},{value:`15_ton`,label:`15 Tonnes`,capacity:15e3},{value:`custom`,label:`Custom`,capacity:null}] - exact, and the study's 'UI only offers 10_ton and 15_ton' is at.filter(e=>e.value!==`custom`), also exact; the custom input really does carry min:100,step:100 as claimed (two occurrences). InventoryView-Bw0D5ewQ.js: b={"GP-FGM":`Gupta Godown Finished Goods`,"BH-FGM":`Jivo Mart · Sonipat`,"GP-FG":`Gupta Godown Basement Finished Godown`,"BH-EC":`Bhakharpur Finished E-Commerce`} - character-exact, including the Mart-vs-Oil warning the study draws from BH-FGM. ShipmentList-G11ipdat.js: z={draft,pending_approval,approved,rejected,dispatched,in_transit,delivered} (7) and V={waiting,email_failed,verified,rejected} (4) - exact. shipmentAPI-DKVOXJWL.js confirms switch_state's `any` sentinel: listSwitching:(e=`any`)=>i(`GET`,`/api/shipment/shipments/?switch_state=${encodeURIComponent(e)}`). DISAGREEMENT WITH LENS C, adjudicated in the study's favour: Lens C restricts `warehouse` to ['GP-FGM'] and calls ALL 'a client-side sentinel, not necessarily accepted'. It is wrong - InventoryView's queryFn is ()=>m.list(e) with the prop defaulting to `ALL`, and m.list is e?`?warehouse=${encodeURIComponent(e)}`:``, so `ALL` being truthy IS transmitted on the wire. Neither is server-confirmed (403), but the study describes what the app actually sends.
impact: None. Also confirmed independently: shipmentAPI's u=`GP-FGM` hardcode, and Record's tonnes=Sigma planned_liters/1e3 which is the basis of Trap 5's ~9% oil overstatement.

claim: `shipment record` `status` enum is {draft, pending_approval, approved, dispatched} with '' for all
evidence: This is the sharpest study-vs-LensC disagreement and the STUDY IS RIGHT. Record-uhJVTCfL.js has THREE vocabularies and Lens C picked the wrong one. The tab list feeding the API is g=[`all`,`draft`,`pending_approval`,`approved`,`dispatched`,`deleted`], the call is u.record({status:k===`all`?``:k}) guarded by if(k!==`deleted`) - so the wire values are exactly draft/pending_approval/approved/dispatched plus empty-string, and `deleted` never reaches the endpoint, precisely as the study says. Lens C instead published enum ['shipped','short','not_loaded'], which is h={shipped,short,not_loaded} - a CLIENT-SIDE line-status filter read from the browser query string (useState(()=>{let e=V.get(`filter`);return[`shipped`,`short`,`not_loaded`].includes(e)?e:`all`})). Tellingly, Lens C's own note describes the study's enum ('all is sent as the empty string... a deleted tab exists but short-circuits before the call') while its enum array contradicts that note.
impact: If a spec author trusts Lens C here, `shipment record --status shipped` ships as a legal flag that the backend has never been sent and that names a line-level concept, not a shipment status. The study prevents that.
action: No change to the study. Flag harvest/lensC-params.jsonl's /api/shipment/record/ record as WRONG so it is not merged.

claim: `shipment appointment-items` has 12 query params
evidence: It has 13, and the study's own §4 list actually names all 13 - only the count is wrong. Counted from shipmentAPI-DKVOXJWL.js getItems verbatim: truck_size, truck_capacity_liters, priority_premium_pct, priority_commodity_pct, priority_other_pct, priority_strict, maximize_fill, respect_stock, appointment_ids, selected_pos, product_family, family_asins, commit_caps_json = 13. Lens C also lists 13. The '12' appears twice (§2 endpoint table and §4 note) and once more in the confidence summary. Separately, the confidence summary says the doh-auto-fill names are 'Verbatim from the SPA's URLSearchParams builders' - imprecise: dohAutoFill's builder is generic (new URLSearchParams(Object.entries(e).filter(([,e])=>e))), and the 8 names come from a caller object literal in CreateShipment-jeq_xTG5.js: {truck_size:i,...a?{truck_capacity_liters:a}:{},...Nt?{fc:Nt}:{},...Je?{priority_strict:`1`}:{},maximize_fill:$e?`1`:`0`,...o?{priority_premium_pct,priority_commodity_pct,priority_other_pct}:{}}. The 8 names are right; the sourcing sentence is not.
impact: Cosmetic - no param is missing or invented. But a spec reviewer counting the table against the prose will find a mismatch and lose confidence in the rest, which would be undeserved.
action: Change '12 observed query params' to 13 in all three places. Reword the doh-auto-fill confidence line to 'verbatim from the caller's request object in CreateShipment-jeq_xTG5.js; dohAutoFill itself takes a generic object and drops falsy values'.

claim: Exclusion count: §2 says '9 excluded (§5)' while §5 is headed 'Ten endpoints'
evidence: Internal inconsistency, though both numbers are defensible. The bundle has 34 endpoints: 22 with a SHIPPED_COMMAND_NAME plus 12 without. The study publishes 25 (22 shipped + 3 new: appointment-families, fc-switch-group, po-appointments - I confirmed all 3 genuinely lack a shipped name, so they are additions, not renames). 34 - 25 = 9 in-bundle exclusions, which is §2's number. §5's table has 10 rows because it adds /api/shipment/shipments/{id}/switch/email/, which the study itself flags as 'Not in the bundle'. So the arithmetic resolves, but the text never says so.
impact: Low. A reviewer reconciling §2 against §5 hits an apparent off-by-one in the most safety-critical section of the study (the write denylist).
action: §2 should read '9 in-bundle exclusions plus 1 found outside the bundle - 10 total, see §5.'

claim: `master products` and `upload master-sheet` return the same 907 rows
evidence: Both live payloads report exactly 907 (probe-run1.jsonl: /api/master/products rows 907 / 15,596 B; /api/upload/master-sheet rows 907 / 11,615 B). Row-by-row the first three match in the same order and are identical on every overlapping field. Row 1: products {format AMAZON, format_sku_code B0CYH9N7YW, product_name '200 ml (Pack of 6) (Apple Sugar Free', item APPLE 200ML, sku_sap_code FG0000258, sku_sap_name 'GLASS BOTTLE 200 MLS APPLE 12 PCS', case_pack 1, per_unit '200 MLS', per_unit_value null, tax_rate 0.05, uom MLS, item_head OTHER} vs master-sheet, same 12 values plus row_id (28,55). Rows 2 (GINGER ALE 200ML / FG0000238) and 3 (MOJITO 200ML / FG0000244) likewise. Column arithmetic checks out: products has 12 fields, master-sheet has 20 keys = 19 declared columns + row_id, and the delta is exactly the 7 the study names (category, sub_category, brand, category_head, is_litre, is_litre_oil, packaging_cost); every one of products' 12 is present in master-sheet. The study's own ~93% caveat ('not proven for all 907') is the honest framing and should stay.
impact: None - correctly established, and the guidance ('same 907 rows, different column sets') is the right thing to put in CLI help.

claim: `row_id` is a Postgres ctid on master-sheet and ads-master but an integer on pincode-mapping
evidence: Straight from the live payloads. master-sheet: "(28,55)", "(41,5)", "(41,6)" - note the page number jumps 28 -> 41, which is ctid behaviour and not any kind of sequence. ads-master: "(0,24)","(0,25)","(0,26)","(0,27)","(0,29)" - (0,28) is skipped, i.e. a dead tuple, which is further corroboration. pincode-mapping: "3928","894","6299","1435","5882","2876" - plain integers, and notably NOT sorted (the rows are ordered by state/city while the ids are scattered), so it behaves like a real surrogate key. One pedantic correction: pincode-mapping's row_id is a JSON *string* containing an integer ("3928"), not a JSON number - relevant if the CLI types the column.
impact: None on the substance. The 'never persist a row_id from master-sheet or ads-master' warning is correct and worth keeping prominent.
action: Add half a sentence: pincode-mapping's row_id is transmitted as a quoted string, so do not declare it an int in the spec.

claim: Four out-of-bundle write endpoints exist: /api/upload/delete-by-date, /api/upload/fk-grocery-master, /api/upload/flipkart-grocery/reprocess, POST /api/shipment/shipments/{}/switch/email/
